The uninstaller checks whether its registered executable path exists and tries a `SysWOW64` path when it does not. The Windows app record references the updated install and uninstall scripts. Other uninstall behavior remains unchanged. **Possibly related issues** - `fleetdm/fleet#57152`: The issue describes a mismatch between a `SysWOW64` uninstaller location and a registered `system32` path. This change adds a fallback for that path mismatch in the Smartsheet uninstall script. **Severity of issue fixed:** Medium
Merge Risk: Moderate · up to b0b42

The fallback improves legacy uninstall handling, but cleanup can still target a stale directory or run after uninstall failure. Reconcile the cleanup path and skip deletion after failure before merging.

Full details: Title check

**Explanation** The title names the main change: Smartsheet (Windows) install and uninstall now use machine-wide scope. The install script adds /allusers, and the uninstall script adds a SysWOW64 fallback for machine-wide installs. The title is specific and matches the changeset. The 'fix(fma)' prefix is a conventional-commit style scope, which is acceptable.
Full details: Description check

**Explanation** The description follows the template structure. It links the issue (Fixes `#58023`), explains the root cause and both script changes, and lists the changed files. The checklist is filled in with testing notes. It includes the required AI section with tool and model. Some template items are unchecked or not addressed (changes file box is unchecked, automated tests box unchecked, manual QA not done, and it does not mention the Frontend, database, Apple MDM, or fleetd sections). These are either not applicable to this change or are explicitly noted as untested, so the description is mostly complete.
Full details: Linked Issues check

**Explanation** Directly linked issue `#58023` has two coding requirements. (1) Install machine-wide, as declared by installer_scope "machine". The reviewed head sets ArgumentList = "/S /allusers" in ee/maintained-apps/inputs/winget/scripts/smartsheet_install.ps1, replacing the bare /S that caused the per-user install into SYSTEM's profile. (2) Uninstall through Fleet must remove the app. The reviewed head adds a fallback in smartsheet_uninstall.ps1. When the parsed uninstall exe is missing, the script replaces \system32\ with \SysWOW64\ and uses the redirected path if it exists. This matches the path in the issue (C:\WINDOWS\system32\config\systemprofile\...). The change is in the same form as the Zettlr fallback in zettlr_uninstall.ps1. The closed issue `#57159` is background only. Residual uncertainty: the installer switch behavior and the uninstall fallback were not run on Windows. Also, the uninstall script acts on the first registration it finds (HKCU, then HKLM, then WOW6432Node). On a host that has both a stranded SYSTEM copy and a new machine-wide registration, one run removes only the first match. That case is not in the reported failure, so it does not fail this requirement.
Full details: Out of Scope Changes check

**Explanation** The changed files are smartsheet_install.ps1 (install switch and comment), smartsheet_uninstall.ps1 (SysWOW64 path fallback), and outputs/smartsheet/windows.json (install_script_ref, uninstall_script_ref, and matching refs entries).
